text: A bomb was an explosive device. Types of bomb included: ammonia bomb, anti-matter bomb, atomic compression bomb, baradium bomb, cluster bombs such as the CL-3 antistarfighter cluster bomb and the magnepulse bomb, concussion bomb, core bomb, disruptor bomb, electro-proton bomb, energy bomb, flash bomb, gas bomb, glop bomb, gravity bomb, incremental-sequence bomb, ion bomb, Jedi shadow bomb, the M-12, neutron bomb, nuclear bombs such as the fission bomb, parasite bomb, plague bomb, plasma bomb, pressure bomb, proton bomb, radiation bomb, talking bomb, thermal bomb, thermite bomb, thought bomb, time bombs such as the TB-47 time bomb, tow-cable bomb, the XG Anti-Gravity Field Bomb, and the Zicx-bug bomb. The Immobilizer 418 cruiser Bomb was named after the explosive device.
title: Bomb/Legends — introduction

text:
A ray shield was a common type of deflector shield. It was designed to absorb blasts from energy weapons such as laser cannons and turbolasers. Ray shields absorbed much of the impact of the weapon's strike, rocking the ship and scoring the underlying armor plating.

The energy requirements for ray shields was tremendous; as such, they were only raised when combat was expected. The ray shield permeated the hull, sheathing the vessel in layers of energy. The shield could extend out from the hull by millimeters or a few centimeters, and was so powerful that it was often fatal to anyone who came into contact with it.
title: Ray shield/Legends — introduction

text:
The Rimma Trade Route was one of the major routes that crossed the galaxy. It started at Abregado-rae in the Core Worlds, and went all the way to the Kathol sector in the far reaches of the Outer Rim Territories.

An important branch of the Rimma, the Shapani Bypass, grew increasingly important in later years, and some considered it part of the Rimma for all practical purposes.

Another branch, which was a continuation of the Rimma, was the Trition Trade Route. The Trition began at Karideph and continued on into the Kathol sector.
title: Rimma Trade Route/Legends — introduction
